evidence_quotes.two_concerns_question: I know most of our customers have usually two concerns when moving the first, the movers being on time or to damage their items when being moved are any of those a concern with moving with us?
evidence_quotes.two_layers_deep: N/A — customer immediately stated no concerns and offered strong praise instead.
evidence_quotes.value_days: Right and then for the four hours, I would like to budget at $863 and that's for the $192, an hourly rate two movers $192 for Saturday... and then Monday is $192... Let's do Monday. That'll work.
evidence_quotes.rate_lock_then_ask: Never asked. Rep moved directly to email send and generic close: 'And then I will send everything over via email. And then do you have any questions or concerns for me?'

top_strength: Brianne asked the two-concerns question early and before any probing, set a realistic time and scope estimate that matched the customer's own assessment, and handled the value-day pricing comparison by showing the actual dollar savings ($8/hour) and confirming the customer's preference.
coaching_note: Step 3 (Two Promises) and Step 7 (Ask for the Business) were completely skipped — no on-time guarantee or damage coverage was stated despite the customer's prior experience, and no explicit ask for the move was ever made; the call ended with a generic 'any questions?' and a vague email send, leaving zero commitment on the table.
